newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Death toll in Pakistani bus crash rises to 24.
newsitem.headline: Death toll in Pakistani bus crash rises to 24.

text.p: At least 24 people, 19 of them soldiers, were killed and four injured when a bus plunged into a valley in northern Pakistan, a bus company official said on Sunday.
Muhammad Naseem, transport manager of the Gilgit-based Northern Areas Transport Corporation, told Reuters 28 people had been aboard the bus when it crashed on Saturday.

He said rescuers had recovered 21 bodies from the wreckage of the bus, which had hurtled 300 feet (100 metres) from the twisting road into a dry ravine. Three bodies remained trapped under the wreckage.
"It was either brake failure or the driver fell asleep because there were no tyre marks on the road," Naseem said.

All the soldiers had been on their way from the northeastern town of Skardu to Rawalpindi, near Islamabad, a journey of about 290 km (181 miles). They had just been paid and were going on leave, Naseem added.
